title: Authorization Synchrony and Audit Scoping — Runway for Delegated Operations
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary

This playbook defines the Authorization Synchrony model and prescriptive Audit Scoping guidance for delegated model operations and multi-region deployments. It ties together RBAC change propagation, CI/CD gating in the secure SDLC, audit log scoping and retention, data-residency markers, incident detection for entitlement drift, and packaging of compliance evidence for external audits. The goal is predictable, auditable authorization state throughout a service lifecycle while minimizing noise in compliance artifacts.

Who should read this

- Security engineers responsible for RBAC governance and entitlement controls
- Platform and SRE teams operating multi-tenant inference clusters
- Release engineers and owners of CI/CD gates in the secure SDLC
- Compliance and legal contacts preparing evidence for external audits

Context and motivation

In distributed deployments (hosted, dedicated, private), authorization state is created and modified by multiple systems: admin consoles, automation, CI/CD, identity syncs, and emergency fixes. Without a single-source-of-truth synchrony model, audits surface inconsistent entitlements, retention gaps, and confusing evidence bundles. This playbook provides a defensible pattern for:

- Ensuring RBAC updates are synchronized and traceable across control plane components
- Scoping which audit events are required for compliance objectives and which are retained as operational telemetry
- Propagating residency and retention metadata through entitlement change events so evidence satisfies cross-border requirements

Key concepts

1) Authorization Synchrony (AuthSync): a pattern that requires each entitlement change to be recorded as a single authoritative event (AuthEvent) in the system of record. Downstream systems consume the AuthEvent rather than applying independent changes.

2) Audit Scopes: classification of audit events into three tiers for retention and packaging: Compliance (regulatory proof), Operational (SRE/debugging), and Ephemeral (high-volume telemetry).

3) Residency Token: a small metadata token attached to AuthEvent and related audit entries indicating regional residency, legal hold flags, and maximum retention TTL. This token follows evidence through export and packaging.

Ownership and SLAs

- AuthSync ownership: Identity & Access (identity-access@redwood.ai) — SLA: 2 business days for triage of sync failures.
- Audit export & packaging: Compliance Engineering — SLA: 5 business days for generating an auditor-ready evidence bundle for incidents marked high-priority.
- SDLC gating for entitlements: Release Engineering — enforcement at pre-merge CI gates.

AuthEvent schema (required fields)

All entitlement changes MUST be emitted as an AuthEvent and conform to the following minimal JSON schema when persisted to the AuthEvent store and audit log. The example below is required for compliance packaging.

Example (persisted event payload):

{"event_id":"uuid-v4","timestamp":"2026-03-01T18:22:00Z","actor":"svc:entitlement-sync/ci-bot","action":"grant","resource":"model-serving/pool-prod-42","role":"inference:invoke","change_reason":"canary-rollout:customer-123","residency_token":"eu:legal-hold:false:ttl=730d","trace_id":"4f2a1c...","correlation_ids":["deploy-2026-03-01-42"]}

(When emitting events, ensure fields are strings; complex metadata should be encoded as short tokens as above.)

Audit Scoping matrix

| Audit Tier | Examples | Retention | Export format for compliance |
|------------|----------|-----------|-----------------------------|
| Compliance | Role grants/revokes, approval decisions, emergency privilege activations, JIT activations | Min 7 years or jurisdictional requirement | Signed bundle (WORM) with residency token metadata (JSON + CSV index) |
| Operational | Periodic entitlement reconciliation reports, sync status, CI gate logs | 90 days (default) | NDJSON slice suitable for SRE investigation |
| Ephemeral | High-volume telemetry (cache hits, sync heartbeats) | 30 days | Aggregated metrics; not included in compliance bundles |

Minimum thresholds and alerts

- If the AuthEvent store records > 200 role changes per minute for a single tenant region continuously for 10 minutes, raise SEV-2 to Identity & Access (pager) — probable misconfiguration or automated exploit.
- If an entitlement change is applied by a downstream consumer without a corresponding AuthEvent within 60s, mark as "sync-mismatch" and increment reconciliation counter. If mismatch rate > 0.1% of applied changes in 24h, open an incident.

Procedures

A) Authoritative change flow (normal ops)

1. Change originates through one of the approved actors: admin console, automated CI job, delegated service with proper client certificate.
2. Actor writes an AuthEvent to the AuthEvent API (POST /auth/v1/events). AuthEvent must be signed by the actor's service key.
3. AuthEvent is validated and stored in the AuthEvent stream (system of record). Event id returned to actor.
4. Change propagation: downstream services subscribe to AuthEvent stream and apply mapped grants/revokes deterministically.
5. Post-change reconciliation job validates applied state against AuthEvent after 2 minutes. Any divergence triggers an automatic rollback attempt if the change was a revoke; otherwise, raises an alert.

B) Emergency entitlements (SEV workflow)

1. Operator requests temporary elevation via the emergency-privs endpoint (POST /auth/v1/emergency-request) including justification and TTL.
2. Request is pre-authorized by two-person on-call approval (explicit yes from two separate identities) OR proof of existing runbook clause.
3. System emits an AuthEvent with residency_token including legal-hold=true if required. Emergency grants auto-expire at TTL and must generate a compliance incident package on expiry.

C) CI/CD gating (SDLC integration)

- Any PR that changes entitlement rules (YAML in infra/) must include:
  1) unit tests for policy parsing
  2) a simulation run that emits a dry-run AuthEvent bundle to the pre-production AuthEvent stream
  3) a signed approver (security/release) binding for the merge commit

If a simulation shows > 1% increase in effective privilege surface for any customer, block the merge and require mitigation.

Reconciliation and evidence packaging

- Daily reconciliation runs produce three artifacts: reconciliation-report.ndjson, unmatched-applied-changes.csv, and reconciliation-signature.txt (SHA256 + signer). These are the building blocks of compliance evidence.
- Evidence bundle layout for audits:
  - manifest.json (top-level index)
  - events/compliance.ndjson (Compliance-tier events)
  - events/operational.ndjson (Operational-tier events)
  - exports/signatures/ (signatures and key references)
  - residency-map.csv (region -> retention policy mapping)

A small manifest example:

{
  "bundle_id":"bundle-2026-03-01-0001",
  "created_by":"compliance-automation@redwood.ai",
  "coverage_window":"2026-02-01T00:00:00Z/2026-03-01T00:00:00Z",
  "residency_flags":"eu:us:apac",
  "sha256_index":"..."
}

(Manifest should be produced as top-level JSON; bundles are stored in WORM-backed storage.)

Export CLI examples

# export compliance-tier events for tenant 'customer-123' in EU region for last 30 days
redwood-cli auth export --tenant customer-123 --region eu --tier compliance --since 2026-02-01 --out ./evidence/bundle-2026-02

# generate signed manifest
redwood-cli auth sign-bundle --path ./evidence/bundle-2026-02 --kms-key projects/redwood/keys/compliance-signing --out manifest.json

Data residency handling

- All AuthEvents must include a residency_token. Residency_token propagation rules:
  - If the change originates from a control plane in-region, the token inherits region code (e.g., 'us', 'eu').
  - If the change affects a resource that is region-tagged (model-serving/pool-prod-42[europe]), the residency token must include the region and applicable retention TTL.
  - When exporting bundles for multi-region audits, the compliance export process must separate events by region folder to match legal hold requirements.

Incident response integration (entitlement drift)

Detection signals:
- Reconciliation delta > 100 entitlements for a tenant in a 1h window.
- Unexpected application of a high-privilege role without corresponding AuthEvent.
- Large-scale JIT activation rates (> 50 activations/min across customers).

Triage steps:
1. Assign incident owner (Identity SRE) and set severity per incident runbook.
2. Snapshot current AuthEvent stream (WORM) and lock write access to the affected resource(s).
3. Export compliance-tier events for the 24h window and produce an evidence bundle with residency token separation.
4. If compromise suspected, perform credential rotation and revoke long-lived tokens; document actions as subsequent AuthEvents.

Evidence chain-of-custody notes

- All evidence bundles MUST include signature files and a signer identity. Key material used for signing should be recorded in the manifest with key id and rotation timestamp.
- Access to evidence bundles is audited via the audit-logs service; any access must be a Compliance-tier event and retained for the same retention period.

Implementation checklist (minimum viable enforcement)

- [ ] AuthEvent API (POST /auth/v1/events) implemented and used by admin console and automation
- [ ] AuthEvent store configured with region-aware retention and WORM export capability
- [ ] CI/CD gate requires dry-run AuthEvent simulation for entitlement changes
- [ ] Daily reconciliation job producing required artifacts and signatures
- [ ] Pager integration for AuthSync mismatch thresholds and high-change-rate alerts
- [ ] Compliance export tooling with residency-aware separation and signed manifests

Appendix A — Operational example: diagnosing a sync-mismatch

Step-by-step:
1. Alert: reconciliation counter shows 120 sync-mismatch events in 24h for tenant customer-123 (threshold 10).
2. Owner (Identity SRE) retrieves the reconciliation-report.ndjson and unmatched-applied-changes.csv.
3. Run the quick-check script to map applied changes to AuthEvents:

python tools/auth_reconcile.py --report reconciliation-report.ndjson --applied unmatched-applied-changes.csv --out findings.json

4. If findings.json contains 'applied_without_authevent' entries, identify the service applying changes and quarantine it by switching to read-only mode via feature flag: feature-flag set serviceX.entitlement-apply=false

Appendix B — Policy excerpts (acceptable justification list for emergency grants)

- P1: Customer-facing outage requiring immediate revoke/grant to restore service (must include incident id).
- P2: Regulatory request with signed legal approval (document id).
- P3: Confirmed vulnerability exploitation in a single process path.
